Use a **partial update**, typically with `PATCH`, and apply only the fields the client actually sent.

**How it works:**

1. **Make every field optional in the update model.** The input model is still validated. So, if you want to receive partial updates that can omit all the attributes, you need to have a model with all the attributes marked as optional (with default values or `None`).[1]
2. **Load the stored profile** into a Pydantic model.
3. **Extract only the sent fields** with `item.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`. This way you can update only the values actually set by the user, instead of overriding values already stored with default values in your model.[1]
4. **Merge the changes.** Create a copy of the stored model, updating its attributes with the received partial updates (using the `update` parameter).[1]
5. **Save and return** the updated model.

```python
@app.patch("/items/{item_id}")
async def update_item(item_id: str, item: Item) -> Item:
    stored_item_data = items[item_id]
    stored_item_model = Item(**stored_item_data)
    update_data = item.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    updated_item = stored_item_model.model_copy(update=update_data)
    items[item_id] = jsonable_encoder(updated_item)
    return updated_item
```

**Why not just replace the whole record?** Unsent fields get overwritten with defaults. For example, if a body omits a stored `"tax": 20.2`, the input model would take the default value of `"tax": 10.5`.[2]

**Notes:**
- `PATCH` isn't required. You can actually use this same technique with an HTTP `PUT` operation.[1]
- If you're using SQLModel, the same idea applies: call `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`, then use `hero_db.sqlmodel_update(hero_data)` to update the `hero_db` with the data from `hero_data`.[4]
- To keep a separate model with required fields for creating profiles, you can use the ideas described in [Extra Models](extra-models.md).[1]
